welcome_lead: Today you'll feel the grip of the SS, the Gestapo and Goebbels' propaganda.
meta_desc: GCSE History — SS, Gestapo, propaganda and Nazi control.
final_note: You learned how the Nazis built total control through terror and media.

walkthroughs.body_html:
After the Night of Long Knives in 1934, Himmler's SS ran terror.

The Gestapo tapped phones, opened mail and relied on tip-offs from neighbours and blockwarts. The People's Court tried political opponents — judges in red robes guaranteed Nazi verdicts.

Joseph Goebbels ran the Reich Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda from March 1933.

Cheap Volksempfänger radios reached 70% of homes by 1939. Newspapers, films and the 1936 Berlin Olympics projected Aryan glory. Books by Jews and communists were burned in May 1933.

The first camp, Dachau, opened in March 1933 for political prisoners.

By 1939 there were six major camps. The Church was muzzled by the 1933 Concordat with the Pope. Protestant 'Reich Church' united churches under Nazi control — though pastors like Niemöller resisted.

mcqs.q: Which was the first concentration camp?
How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
Peel created the police to fight the French during the Napoleonic Wars.

mcqs.q: What was the political significance of the Reichstag Fire?
options: Peel created the police to fight the French during the Napoleonic Wars.
Hitler used it to issue the Reichstag Fire Decree suspending civil liberties, jail Communists, and create the conditions for the Enabling Act of March 1933.
The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
Hitler personally set the fire and blamed it on the Communists.

mcqs.q: Why did Robert Peel create the Metropolitan Police in 1829?
options: The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
Industrial London's crime, poor watchmen, and fear of disorder pushed Peel to create a professional, uniformed but unarmed force focused on crime prevention.
Peel created the police because there had been no law enforcement of any kind before 1829.
Peel created the police to fight the French during the Napoleonic Wars.
